terms.gloss: the year’s produce; the price of grain and provisions
terms.comment: Annōna cāra est, food is dear; vīlis annōna, cheap food. The word is the market price, so it is high or low, not large or small.

terms.grammar: laxō used intransitively, with annōna as subject
evidence: Liv. 2.34.12: annōnam laxāre, to bring the price down (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman gives the passive laxārī for prices going down; Livy has the active, intransitive with annōna, or transitive, “bring the price down”.

phrases.latin: Multa, sī annōna in macellō nōn nimia est.
phrases.english: Many things, if the price of food at the market is not too high.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 322.
